title: Meta’s Muse reportedly keeps files on everyone you love
key_facts: Muse, Meta's AI assistant, has more than 5 million downloads in 3 weeks.
A report from Wired and AI safety researcher Karan Joshi says Muse has been instructed to create "a page for every person in the user's life".
A "Relationships" loop runs hourly in the background on a user's computer to update each page, per researchers at FutureSociety.
Joshi told Wired he got Muse to reveal its system prompts; Mashable cannot verify them, but other researchers have shared the alleged prompts online.
Pages cover family, friends, partners, colleagues and followed accounts, built from messages, photos and past interactions, including what the user owes or has promised.
Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts told Wired Muse compiles context "based on public information and from what you've chosen to share" under the permissions the user grants.
Mashable notes Apple's recent statement on changing Full Disk Access because of agents like Muse.
quote_evidence: Namely, the report claimed that Muse has been instructed to create "a page for every person in the user’s life."
Mashable cannot independently verify these system instructions, but Joshi isn't the only researcher to share the alleged prompts online in recent days.
“Muse gathers that based on public information and from what you’ve chosen to share,”
why_it_matters_hint: People who never used Muse could still be profiled by it, if the leaked prompts are genuine.
event_date: Wired report first carried in our 4 Oct 2026 edition; Mashable article 9 Oct 2026
notes: Repeat of the WIRED story in our 4 Oct 2026 edition (item 31); Mashable adds the 5 million downloads and the Apple link. System prompts are unverified.
